newsitem.title: UK: Euro-bourses rise but wary of U.S. jobs data.
newsitem.headline: Euro-bourses rise but wary of U.S. jobs data.

text.p: European share markets built on their record closes on Friday and the dollar hit its highest levels in years against the yen and mark, but investors kept a wary eye on crucial U.S. jobs data due later.

All three of Europe's major bourses showed rises, with Frankfurt and Paris hitting trading highs, after U.S. blue-chips drove the Dow Industrial average to a 26 point rise on upbeat retail sales data.

The dollar started on a strong footing in Europe, hitting its highest level in years against the mark and yen on a strengthening perception that the world's main industrialised nations will not try to shoot down the U.S. currency at this weekend's meeting in Berlin of Group of Seven (G7) finance ministers and central bank governors.

The U.S. currency rose to 1.6609 marks in early trade, its highest level since June 1994, against 1.6515 in late European trade on Thursday. Against the yen, it hit a four-year peak of 124.38, up from its late Thursday level of 123.83.
But analysts said the market appeared loath to push the dollar much higher ahead of U.S. employment data due later at 1330 GMT and the G7 meeting.
U.S. non-farm payrolls, key data for indicating the strength of the U.S. economy, are forecast to have risen 237,000 in January after an increase of 262,000 in December.
Chase Securities said it expected the payrolls figure to be boosted by a smaller-than-normal decline in seasonal employment, helped by a mild winter.
German debt climbed in early trading, supported by ongoing sluggish German economic conditions, but British government bonds opened a little lower with traders waiting for the U.S. figures.
One broker said a payroll rise of less than 220,000 should allow bond markets to head higher.
Equity markets were all bolstered by Wall Street's renewed strength following Wednesday's 86-point slide, but investors looked unwilling to make any significant moves before the jobs data.
"We've had a good run and we're in for a period of consolidation at best," commented one London dealer as the blue-chip FTSE 100 index rose nearly 14 points to 4,279.7 by mid-morning..
"We are definitely looking tired," said another "It's a struggle as the index approaches the 4,300 mark."

The continuing strength of the pound was also adding to concern. The Bank of England's trade-weighted index moved on Thursday to its highest level since the pound left Europe's exchange rate mechanism in 1992.
French stocks hit a fresh all time high of 2,572 points on the CAC-40 index before slipping slightly to 2,571 for a rise of 13 points by 1030 GMT.

Havas , suspended on Thursday, opened 1.71 percent lower at 441.30 francs and then lost another 10 francs by mid-morning. Generale des Eaux , also suspended on Thursday, opened up 2.18 percent at 750 and then surged to 772 francs for a rise of more than five percent.

The companies announced on Thursday that CGE would become the majority shareholder of Havas with 30 percent, and Havas would become the leading shareholder in Canal Plus with 34.4 percent as part of a restructuring of their media activities.
German shares also surged to a new record in bourse trade, buoyed by the dollar climbing to 1.66 marks and a stable German debt market.
Traders said the market had shaken off worries about profit-taking and would seek to extend gains ahead of the U.S. jobs data.
The 30-share DAX was up 26.53 points at 3,130.67 points after hitting a peak of 3,137.07.
Veba slipped from its day's high to show a rise of 75 pfennigs at 92.25 after Britain's C&W backed out of a telecoms alliance.
CURRENCIES AT 1030 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6598 marks and 124.33 yen compared with 1.6514 marks and 123.70 yen in late European trading on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1030 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 13.8 points, or 0.32 percent, at 4,279.7.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 13.22 points, or 0.52 percent, at 2,571.65.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 26.53 points, or 0.85 percent, at 3,130.67.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $340.90 against $342.80 previously, the lowest fix since April 22, 1993. Silver was two cents down at $4.80.
